To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
breast carcinomas frequently express cancer testis ( CT ) genes, and that antibodies to CT antigens occur at low frequency in the sera of these patients.

(a) breast carcinomas are one of the most frequently CT gene‐expressing cancers, (b) CT genes are coexpressed frequently, (c) antibody responses to NY‐ESO-1 and SCP-1 are detectable in 4% and 6%, respectively, of patients and (d) there is no correlation of CT gene expression or antibody responses with clinical parameters.

the expression of cancer‐testis genes in breast cancer is frequent, but not correlated to the clinical outcome, and that the expression of these genes is not associated with an immune response against the encoded proteins.

the identification of cancer‐associated antigens and the characterization of the cellular and molecular basis of the immune response to these antigens in patients with cancer.

breast cancers are among the tumors that most frequently express CT genes, and that a large proportion of these tumors are likely to elicit immune responses against CT antigens.
breast carcinomas express a wide spectrum of CT antigens with a high frequency of expression, but that there are only few patients who express a high number of CT antigens.
the results of the studies on the expression of CT genes in breast cancer are not conclusive and that the expression of CT gene products is not a reliable prognostic factor for breast cancer.

breast carcinomas express many cancer‐testis antigens.
